matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and compare the left‑hand side with the right‑hand side to find the difference.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick equation, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: XIX = XII + II gives 19 vs 14, discrepancy = 5.

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all Roman‑numeral characters that can be obtained by adding or removing a single matchstick from each character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate possible one‑stick changes for each numeral.
matchstick.example: X can become V by removing a diagonal; I can become II by adding a vertical.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, ensure the character you took it from remains a valid Roman numeral or operator, and the character you add it to also becomes valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before accepting it.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X yields V, which is valid; adding it to another character must keep that character valid.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: A diagonal stick can be moved from a V to make an X (value +5) or removed from an X to make a V (value -5).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy is a multiple of 5, consider converting X↔V.
matchstick.example: XIX → XIV by moving a diagonal from the rightmost X to turn it into V.

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates II (value +1); removing a vertical from II yields I (value -1).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is 1 or -1, try adding or removing a vertical stick from an I/II.
matchstick.example: II → I by removing a vertical stick, decreasing the value by 1.

matchstick.title: Operator change – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical turns it into a minus sign, and adding a vertical to a minus creates a plus.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic sign needs to change sign, consider converting + ↔ – by moving a vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Changing + to – reduces the right‑hand side by twice the added term.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their original orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical or horizontal, and vice versa.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick relocation, ensure the moved stick’s orientation matches the target character’s required orientation.
matchstick.example: A diagonal from X can only become part of another diagonal character (V or X), not a vertical I.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, recompute the integer values of the whole equation to verify that it now holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any proposed transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After turning XIX into XIV, recompute 14 = 12 + 2, which is true.

matchstick.title: Match discrepancy with possible value changes
matchstick.principle: After computing the numeric discrepancy, prioritize single‑stick transformations whose value change exactly equals the discrepancy (or its negative).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after computing the discrepancy, before enumerating all transformations.
matchstick.example: Discrepancy of 5 suggests trying X↔V (±5) before other moves.

matchstick.title: Operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Horizontal or vertical sticks can be moved between operators (e.g., from ‘=’ to ‘-’) or from an operator to create a new numeral, provided all resulting symbols stay valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy cannot be fixed by numeral changes alone, consider moving sticks from or to operators.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to a ‘-’ turns ‘=’ into ‘-’ and ‘-’ into ‘=’.

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: Confusing stick orientation when visualizing characters.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always check the orientation of the stick before reusing it; diagonals stay diagonal.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: Skipping validation of the source after a stick is taken.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'Validate source and destination characters' principle before finalizing a move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Overlooking operator flexibility in matchstick puzzles.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Include operator change possibilities in the enumeration of transformations.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Relying on visual similarity rather than numeric validation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always re‑evaluate the arithmetic using the 'Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move' skill.

matchstick.description: Assuming the equality sign cannot be altered
matchstick.why_it_happens: Misunderstanding that operators can be changed by stick moves.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Consider horizontal stick relocation involving ‘=’ as part of the operator stick relocation skill.
